claims.text: Metadynamics-driven free-energy minimization at 850°C can steer phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs toward a reproducible equilibrium microstructure.
The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA is multiphase.
Its complex phase boundaries result from prior processing and thermal history.
The proposed metadynamics protocol deposits variable bias potentials every 500 ps for a cumulative duration of 100 ns.
The protocol is conducted at a fixed temperature of 850°C.
Controlled deposition of bias potentials changes the sampled free-energy landscape.
Changes in the free-energy landscape promote transitions from metastable phases to a more stable equilibrium phase configuration.
Periodic deposition of bias potentials fills local free-energy wells.
Filling local free-energy wells removes metastable traps and promotes transformation toward the equilibrium state.
The intervention will minimize metastable phases and cause the microstructure to converge reproducibly to the predicted equilibrium state.
Convergence to the predicted equilibrium microstructure will produce improved and predictable material properties.
Conventional thermal processing without metadynamics typically gives less controllable and less reproducible phase evolution.
The proposed approach is applicable at or near 850°C and on the 100 ns simulation timescale.
Different temperatures or longer processing times may introduce additional complexities.
